correctness.rationale: Subdividing every edge once yields a G-equivariant deleted-product cubical model for unordered two distinct points in any finite tree (at least one edge). For an automorphism of subdivision, fixed vertices and edges form a nonempty subtree with q=k-1, and for g² the same gives s_V=s_E for 2-cycles. Direct orientation-signed fixed-cell traces are L0=C(k,2)+s_V, L1=q(k-2), L2=C(q,2)-sum_fixedv C(f_v,2)-s_E+sum_fixedv t_v. With connected H0=Q and known H_i=0 for i>=2, 1-L0+L1-L2 reduces exactly to sum_v ((f_v-1)(f_v-2)/2-t_v). This equals the exterior-square character of W_v=kernel(sum Q^{incident directions}) at every fixed v. Semisimplicity of rational representations of finite G turns character equality into the asserted noncanonical G-module isomorphism. Independent star-4 direct signed cell counts match the formula at identity, a transposition, a 4-cycle and a double-transposition; finite examples are only corroboration of the all-tree fixed-cell proof.
residual_risks: Averaging traces requires the no higher homology theorem, not just an Euler characteristic; that premise is stated and cited.
Rational representation is noncanonical and cannot be upgraded to integral equivariant splitting.

value.rationale: The formula gives the entire rational symmetry module, not only a familiar tree configuration rank, uniformly for all finite trees and arbitrary vertex-moving automorphisms. Exterior-square augmentation modules give a conceptual local-to-global representation description usable to compute each symmetry trace without constructing the full configuration complex; this is a motivated structural theorem with nontrivial group action.
residual_risks: Two unordered points and rational coefficients only; no integral lattice, more particles or graph cycles.

limitations: The module isomorphism is noncanonical and rational; no higher particle, graph cycle or integral module claim.
Standard higher-homology-vanishing theorem is a published premise rather than rediscovered here.
